chunks: He said: Abu Bakr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Ji'abi reported to me, saying: Abu Nasr Muhammad ibn Umar al-Nishaburi narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Abu al-Sari narrated to us, saying: My father narrated to me, saying: Hafs ibn Ghiyath narrated to us, from Burd ibn Sinan, from Makhul, from Wathilah ibn al-Asqa', who said: The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said:
Do not show gloating over your brother's misfortune, lest God relieve him and afflict you.
And may God bless our master Muhammad, the Prophet, and his family, and grant them peace abundantly.

key_terms.الشماتة: Schadenfreude; malicious joy at another's misfortune. Condemned in Islamic ethics as a sign of spiritual deficiency.
key_terms.يبتليك: To test or afflict; from the root ب-ل-و, denoting divine trial.
key_terms.يعافيه: To grant well-being or relief; from the root ع-ف-و related to pardon and wellness.

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about gloating over others' misfortunes?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) warns against schadenfreude -- taking pleasure in a fellow Muslim's suffering. This teaching, transmitted through the companion Wathilah ibn al-Asqa', emphasizes that divine decree can reverse fortunes: the one who gloats may find himself tested with the very same trial, while the afflicted brother may be granted relief by God. The hadith reinforces the Islamic ethic of empathy and mutual support among believers.
